title: Procurement acceptance + data escrow & onboarding sync
summary: Kickoff to align procurement, legal and security on Redwood onboarding: MSA/DPA redlines, escrow ask for models and logs, SLA tiers, KMS/Egress requirements, and next steps to get to commercial sign-off and pilot. AE + SE covered technical constraints and proposed mitigation (dedicated vs hosted with VPC).
next_steps: Jordan to send annotated MSA/DPA with proposed redline positions by 2026-02-18
Maya to prepare 1-hour dedicated-infra runbook and latency/cost estimate by 2026-02-20
Priya/Tom to summarize top 3 procurement blockers and escalate by 2026-02-23
Set pilot kick-off for week of 2026-03-02 pending redline alignment
action_items: Jordan: Share pricing spreadsheet & escrow reference (link) — due 2026-02-18
Maya: Run quickbench (50k token/day sim) on dedicated config & share results — due 2026-02-20
Tom: Confirm legal requiremnts for escrow and third-party audits — due 2026-02-23
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. We wanted to run through the onboarding acceptance path, the MSA/DPA redlines you flagged, and the escrow ask Sara mentioned in the ticket.
00:12 Priya Singh: Hi Jordan, hi team. We have procurement here, we've got a couple questions: the escrow for models + logs is a bit new for us, and also impact to pricing if we require on-prem or private deployment.
00:25 Jordan Patel: Totally, that's what today's about. Quick agenda: MSA/DPA status, security/keys/egress, SLA tiers and what triggers pricing changes, and then pilot scope. Maya, want to jump into the infra bits?
00:36 Maya Chen: Yeah, sure. Hi all, Maya here, platform SE. We looked at Orion's infra notes and the key asks: VPC peering or private endpoint, bring-your-own-KMS/HSM option, and retention limits for logs. On deployment modes we typically recommend: hosted for fastest time-to-value, dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and private on-prem if regulatorily required. Each has different tradeoffs on cost and latency.
01:02 Sara Ng: For security: we need SOC2 + ISO attestation, audit logs with 7 years retention, and ability to provide a forensic slice on demand. Also the escrow - is Redwood proposing a financial escrow or code/model escrow?
01:18 Jordan Patel: Good question. The customer-requested escrow in the intake was primarily for access to model artifacts and transactional logs in case of a vendor exit. Our standard response is to propose an escrow arrangement with a neutral third party holding a snapshot under pre-defined release conditions. It can be limited to serialized model metadata and encrypted logs. Maya, is there a size/cost impact?
01:34 Maya Chen: There's a modest storage cost. The heavier cost would come if you require on-prem replication for hot-standby; otherwise, archived snapshots pushed quarterly are cheap. Note: some customers prefer encrypted vault keys stored in their KMS rather than handing keys to the escrow agent.
01:52 Tom Alvarez: Legal wants explicit language in the MSA that release conditions are narrowly defined. Also need to ensure DPA covers a list of subprocessors. On the MSA redlines we suggested: narrower indemnity, limited liability carveouts, and stronger audit rights.
02:09 Jordan Patel: Understood. We're open to discuss specific redlines. I'll share an annotated MSA with our counterpositions. Historically we've accepted limited liability caps tied to fees, but we can discuss carveouts for gross negligence.
02:22 Priya Singh: Pricing question — if we go dedicated vs hosted, how does that impact monthly commitment and overage? Do we get burst?
02:31 Jordan Patel: Dedicated is typically a reserved capacity commitment with configurable autoscaling and burst options — you pay a baseline reserved fee, then overage or burst billed at a different rate. We'll include a pricing tab in the spreadsheet that models your expected token volumes. I'll send that after the call.
02:45 Devon Park: From platform: we have latency targets—aim for sub-200ms p50 for short prompts. Have you seen customers hit that on hosted? And can dedicated offer better p99?
02:55 Maya Chen: Hosted can hit sub-200ms p50 on smaller models and shorter contexts; for high-throughput low-p99 latency we recommend dedicated GPU pools tuned for your model and sequence length. Also there are batching tradeoffs — continuous batching improves cost but can increase tail latency. We can provide specific latency/cost curves for your 512-token median and 2k token worst-case workloads.
03:24 Tom Alvarez: We also need KMS controls. We plan to use our own KMS; we don't want Redwood to ever hold plaintext keys. Is BYOK supported?
03:32 Maya Chen: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated we have integrations where keys are customer-managed via supported KMS providers. For hosted there's an option for envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in certain enterprise tiers. We'll include the keys flow diagram in the runbook.
03:45 Sara Ng: About audit logs — we need immutable logs and the ability to export them into our SIEM daily. What's the retention policy and export format?
03:55 Maya Chen: We persist request/response metadata and system traces per the DPA retention window; log exports can be pushed to S3-compatible endpoints or delivered via secure transfer. Formats are JSON with timestamped events. Retention can be configured; we can also provide a dedicated retention policy of 7 years for audit logs but will call out storage costs.
04:18 Priya Singh: On the escrow, procurement is worried about escrow leading to very high fees. Are there standard cost ranges?
04:26 Jordan Patel: Costs vary. If it's just quarterly encrypted snapshots pushed to a neutral escrow with limited access controls, it's low incremental cost. If you require live replication or hot-standby accessible on demand, that drives much higher engineering and hosting costs. We can propose tiered escrow options.
04:44 Sara Ng: Tom, do you need us to define legal triggers for release now or do you want Redwood to propose language?
04:50 Tom Alvarez: I want Redwood to propose draft language first, then we'll mark up. We have internal policy that release is only on bankruptcy, failure to remedy breach after defined cure period, or mutual termination.
05:03 Jordan Patel: Sounds good — Jordan to send MSA/DPA annotated with proposed escrow clause.
05:08 Maya Chen: Small thing: there's a mention in your intake about 'KV cash' — I think that's KV cache, yeah? I just wanted to flag that we may have misunderstood the cache pattern you need.
05:19 Devon Park: Haha, yes that's a typo, it's KV cache. We do significant session caching and want to understand KV cache persistence for long-running sessions.
05:28 Maya Chen: Ok noted. For long-running sessions we recommend pinned KV cache on dedicated instances or using our persistent KV cache service on private deployments; hosted relies on ephemeral caching which is best-effort for cost reasons.
05:44 Priya Singh: Procurement also wanted to confirm SLA language: uptime and latency SLOs, remedies, and credits. We generally don't accept pure best-effort.
05:54 Jordan Patel: We offer SLA tiers in enterprise contracts. Standard hosted comes with a baseline SLA; Dedicated comes with higher SLOs and possible financial credits tied to uptime and request success rate. For latency SLOs, we typically avoid prescriptive tail latency credits because tail latency is heavily workload-dependent, but we can include latency targets and monitoring obligations with runbooks and remediation timelines.
06:19 Tom Alvarez: We need to see the exact credit thermostat — how many minutes of downtime triggers credits and the formula.
06:26 Jordan Patel: We'll include the SLA table in the redline packet. Also note fallback policies: automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model can be part of the resilience playbook if a specific model's capacity is constrained. That helps avoid total outages.
06:43 Sara Ng: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for EU customers and logs to remain in region. Is that supported on hosted?
06:51 Maya Chen: We support region pinning for hosted in many cloud regions; for stricter EU-only requirements we often recommend Dedicated or Private so networking and data residency controls are explicit. Hosted region pinning reduces latency but may have limited capacity profiles.
07:12 Devon Park: On the pilot — what metrics would you suggest we show to get procurement comfortable? Cost per inference, average latency, error rate, and sample quality checks?
07:22 Maya Chen: Yes, pilot metrics: per-route token cost and cost breakdown, p50/p95/p99 latency, success/error rates, and a small eval set to validate quality/regression. We'll instrument with tracing and cost-per-token dashboards in Redwood Console.
07:37 Priya Singh: Is there an obligatory SOC2 attestation date? Our security folks asked for current audit report.
07:44 Jordan Patel: We can provide a SOC2 Type II report for the last cycle, plus ISO cert snapshots upon request. We'll attach those to the security package.
07:52 Tom Alvarez: Because of escrow and audit rights, legal will require an escalation path and a quarterly compliance review meeting for the first year. Is that reasonable?
07:59 Jordan Patel: Yes, we often schedule a quarterly compliance check for enterprise customers, especially with more stringent DPA or escrow arrangements. Luis from CSM will own that cadence.
08:10 Luis Romero: I'll circulate a quarterly compliance meeting invite and the onboarding checklist after the call.
08:17 Priya Singh: One more thing — data deletion and right-to-be-forgotten. We need confirmation on how to delete PII from logs and any model cache.
08:27 Maya Chen: We can support targeted deletion requests. For model fine-tuning we have separate processes; for request logs, we can scrub or purge per retention policy, and for KV cache we can expire sessions on demand. We'll document the request flow and SLAs for deletions.
08:47 Tom Alvarez: Great. Can you also confirm that you don't re-use our data for model training unless explicitly agreed?
08:53 Jordan Patel: Correct. For enterprise contracts we can include a clause that prohibits use of customer prompts/content for model training unless opt-in is explicit. We'll include that in the DPA redlines.
09:04 Priya Singh: Procurement needs a final commercial summary: baseline monthly commitment, expected overage, and an escrow tier cost estimate. Jordan, can you provide a table with scenarios?
09:13 Jordan Patel: Yes. I'll send a scenarios table showing monthly reserved vs hosted pay-as-you-go, plus an escrow tier cost add-on. Also will flag engineering lead times for dedicated and private options.
09:22 Devon Park: Operational question — if we require BYOK and on-prem private endpoints, how long to stand up a pilot environment?
09:30 Maya Chen: For private on-prem it's typically 6-10 weeks depending on procurement of hardware and network setup. For Dedicated in a customer's VPC it's usually 3-5 weeks. Hosted pilot with region pinning can be days to weeks. We'll outline timeline assumptions in the runbook.
09:49 Tom Alvarez: For legal redlines — we'll circulate our initial redline (we already uploaded to the portal). We expect Redwood to return a counter-redline within 3 business days.
09:58 Jordan Patel: A three-day turnaround is doable. We'll aim to return annotated MSA/DPA within that window.
10:05 Priya Singh: Okay that's helpful. One more procurement item: any escrow or audit vendor certs we need to vet?
10:12 Jordan Patel: We'll propose a couple of neutral escrow vendors we work with; their certifications (ISO 27001, SOC2) will be included. If Orion has approved vendors list, we can crosswalk.
10:21 Sara Ng: On the technical note — can we get a sample of your runbook for key rotation + incident response?
10:28 Maya Chen: Yes, I'll attach a runbook with key rotation cadence, emergency key revocation flows, and incident response SLAs. It includes detailed steps for rotating customer-managed keys and how we handle failover.
10:41 Devon Park: If latency SLOs are missed due to cloud provider maintenance, how does that factor into SLA credits?
10:48 Jordan Patel: There are carveouts for third-party outages; the SLA will specify allowed maintenance windows and force majeure clauses. Credits usually exclude scheduled maintenance that was notified per contract.
11:00 Priya Singh: Ok, sounds like we have a path forward. Can we get a summary email with the items you said you'd deliver and the redline timeline?
11:10 Jordan Patel: Absolutely. We'll send: annotated MSA/DPA, pricing scenarios, escrow tier options, runbook and SOC2 docs, and a proposed pilot plan.
11:17 Tom Alvarez: Quick clarifying point — on indemnities: we'll propose a cap tied to 12 months of fees; is that in the usual ballpark?
11:25 Jordan Patel: That's within range of negotiation. We generally see caps between 6–12 months of fees for SaaS contracts; enterprise exceptions are considered case by case. We'll flag it for legal review in the counter-redline.
11:38 Sara Ng: Any competitor risk we should be aware of? We ran a bake-off with ClearInference and we liked Redwood's latency but they offered a simpler escrow/contracting path.
11:47 Jordan Patel: Understood — we'll make sure the proposal highlights the operational runbook and compliance attachments to close that gap.
11:56 Luis Romero: I'll follow up on the compliance cadence and send invites.
12:02 Jordan Patel: Cool. Recap of next steps: Jordan sends annotated MSA/DPA + pricing scenarios by 2026-02-18; Maya sends dedicated infra runbook and quickbench by 2026-02-20; Luis to send compliance cadence and CSM onboarding checklist; customer provides top procurement blockers by 2026-02-23. Anything else?
12:25 Priya Singh: That covers it. Thanks everyone.
12:29 Jordan Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments.
12:33 End of recording.
